clue.text: Charles touching Camilla's next to middle hole …

parts.note: CHAS is the standard written short form of the name Charles

indicators.note: Camilla has seven letters with I in the middle; the letter beside it, before it, is the one wanted

parts.note: the name Camilla, whose letter just before its middle is used

explanation.surface: A smutty royal joke about Prince Charles and Camilla, the opening of a three-clue run of innuendo.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of Camilla is I, and the letter just before it is M.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep gaping opening in the ground, a very large hole.

clue.text: House offers continental cat piss

parts.note: chat is the French for cat
piss is water, and eau is the French for water, the continental sense carrying over

explanation.surface: A house that offers foreign cat urine as its feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French country house or castle.

clue.text: Having other-worldliness is key to Archerism? No

parts.note: A is a musical key
Jeffrey Archer, the novelist peer, was jailed for perjury, so his trademark is a lie
N is the abbreviation for number, written No

explanation.surface: Asks whether lies from another world are the secret of Jeffrey Archer's career.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alien comes from another world, so it has an extraterrestrial quality.

clue.text: Graduate (sociology and other shit) — one who would make himself smart?

definitions.text: one who would make himself smart?

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
SOC is a short form of sociology

indicators.note: other here means the letters of the word are given in some other form

parts.note: taken as written, its letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneer at a sociology graduate trying to look clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like clever or well dressed, but here it is the verb meaning to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A masochist takes pleasure in pain, so would deliberately hurt himself and make his own skin sting.

clue.text: … a deep productive plot: something to make her randy and somewhere to do something about it …

parts.note: oysters are the classic reputed aphrodisiac

parts.words: somewhere to do something about it
parts.note: a bed is where the resulting urge gets acted on

explanation.surface: Continues the royal innuendo: an aphrodisiac and a place to act on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the sea-floor sense: a bed is a plot of ground, and an oyster bed is one deep under water that yields a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: An oyster bed is an underwater patch of seabed where oysters breed and are farmed, so a fruitful plot below the waves.

clue.text: Each little sod's wandering the city

indicators.note: wandering means the letters stray out of order

parts.note: EA is the short form of each, as on price lists
taken as written, letters and all

explanation.surface: Each small rascal is roaming the streets of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is the Black Sea port city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Young Mr Collins is weighed down by small pox

indicators.note: in a down clue, being weighed down by something means having it on top, so the small letter comes first

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
Phil Collins, the Genesis drummer and singer

explanation.surface: A youthful Phil Collins is laid low by a nasty disease.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'weighed down by' puts S on top of the rest; 'pox' is the old slang for the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The pox, or great pox, was the old name for the sexually transmitted disease caused by Treponema bacteria.

clue.text: City "hostess" enthusiastically entertains

indicators.note: entertains means holding within, so the answer is held inside the words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A city escort, 'hostess' in quotes, keenly receives her clients.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of Germany.

clue.text: Go about casually, showing arse, note, on stage

parts.note: bum is British slang for backside
A is a note of the musical scale
a round is a stage of a competition

explanation.surface: Someone lounging about showing their backside on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum around is slang for idling or drifting about aimlessly.

clue.text: See dad buggered on one — entered by Jordan definitively

indicators.note: buggered here means wrecked, so the letters are broken up

parts.note: taken as written, the six letters to be rearranged
A is one, as in a single

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about Jordan, the glamour model Katie Price, and someone's father.
explanation.walkthrough: Jordan is the river, not the model: it flows into this lake and goes no further.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Jordan ends in the Dead Sea, a salt lake with no outlet, so its final destination.

clue.text: … — unreasonable, taking a girl sexually almost on the vertical?

parts.note: 'a bit' is crude slang for a girl seen as a sexual object, as in a bit of stuff
a steep slope is one that is nearly upright

explanation.surface: Ends the innuendo run: a crude complaint about an awkward upright encounter being too much to ask.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is everyday British for a demand or price that is excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something 'a bit steep' is an idiom for saying a charge or request goes beyond what is fair.

clue.text: The country's so flipping protective of a Mowlam

indicators.note: being protective of something means wrapping round it, so the pair goes round the rest
flipping the two-letter word turns it over, so it reads the other way

parts.note: 'so' and 'as' are interchangeable in phrases like 'so far' and 'as far'
taken as written
Mo Mowlam was the Labour Northern Ireland Secretary in the late 1990s

explanation.surface: A Pacific nation said to guard Mo Mowlam, with 'flipping' as a mild British curse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'country's' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoa is an independent island nation in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Women supervisors for whom union is out of the question

definitions.meaning: reads like female managers, but means men who supervise women: harem guards

definitions.text: for whom union is out of the question
definitions.meaning: reads like a ban on joining a trade union, but means sexual union is physically impossible

explanation.surface: Sounds like female bosses barred from joining a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Castrated men traditionally guarded harems; 'union' is sexual, not industrial.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunuchs were castrated attendants placed in charge of a harem's women because they could not seduce them.

clue.text: Guts shown by boozers restricting Henry from having an erection

indicators.note: restricting here means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub, and inns are pubs

indicators.note: Henry is taken away from the word, leaving the rest

parts.note: hard is crude slang for aroused
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Drinkers' bellies on show while a Henry is kept from getting aroused.
explanation.definitionFit: Innards are the internal organs, the entrails, which is what guts means as a plural noun.

clue.text: (& 26/15/19) High on heroin, TV's Jonathan, unable to have a row, is in trouble

parts.note: up means high, as in up in the air
shit is drug slang for heroin
Jonathan Creek is a BBC television mystery series named after its magician-sleuth hero
with nothing to propel a boat by hand, rowing is impossible

explanation.surface: A stoned TV presenter who cannot even pick a fight is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface (an argument) but rhymes with 'go' in the wordplay (rowing a boat).
explanation.definitionFit: Being up a creek without a paddle is a vulgar idiom for being stuck in a hopeless predicament.

clue.text: Attraction of an earnest plea for some rumpy-pumpy

parts.note: rumpy-pumpy is jokey British slang for sex
an appeal is an earnest request

explanation.surface: What makes someone attractive is begging for a romp.
explanation.definitionFit: Sex appeal is the quality of being sexually attractive to others.

clue.text: see13
Monumental tribute to a stiff Mick Jagger?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grave marker for a corpse, a stiff being slang for a dead body
second meaning, punning: the lead singer is the head Rolling Stone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' hints at Private Eye smut but is the slang for a corpse; the question mark flags the pun on the band name.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is the upright memorial slab at a grave, and Jagger heads the Rolling Stones.

clue.text: Artist's jiggling tits sore

indicators.note: jiggling shakes the letters about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, its eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter's bouncing breasts are aching.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Artist is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was a Victorian painter and poet, a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

clue.text: Topless Hague companion, catching cab back, reveals thing

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of, so the vehicle goes inside the name
topless means the top letter of the name is removed

parts.note: Ffion Hague is the wife of the Conservative politician William Hague

indicators.note: back means the word for the vehicle runs the other way

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about a politician's wife going topless in a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' wants a scandal; it only removes the first F of Ffion.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is an idiom for an obsession, which is what a fixation is.

clue.text: Non-PC WPC's quite reasonable bust

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an attractive policewoman, in politically incorrect terms a fair-looking cop
second meaning: an arrest the suspect admits was justified

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a woman's chest; it is the slang for an arrest. A WPC was a woman police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It's a fair cop' is the catchphrase of a criminal conceding a just arrest, and the words can also leer at a pretty officer.

clue.text: see 13
Each short emission shows effective range of one's organ

indicators.note: an emission sends the letters out in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, its letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Innuendo about how far a man's organ can shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ is the ear, not the one the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which a sound can be heard, the reach of the hearing organ.

clue.text: Fraud: maybe Piers Morgan's humiliated

parts.note: a sham is a fraud or fake
Piers Morgan was a newspaper editor, ED, and 'maybe' marks him as an example

explanation.surface: A jibe that Piers Morgan has been shown up as a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shamed is to be disgraced and made to feel humiliation.

clue.text: Force politician Hague's butt into new suit

indicators.note: into means the politician and the end letter go inside the reworked letters
new tells us the letters of suit are made over afresh

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement
a butt is an end, so the last letter of the name Hague is wanted

explanation.surface: Forcing a Tory leader's backside into a fresh suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or momentum behind something.

clue.text: Yard briefly to OK laundered capital

indicators.note: laundered money is reworked to hide it, so the letters are rearranged
briefly means the word is cut down to just its first letter

parts.note: the word Yard, cut to its opening letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard approving the money-laundering of capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, which suits 'laundered'; it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo is the capital city of Japan.

clue.text: Pushy type: "Let's break in Ben"

indicators.note: in tells us the reworked letters go inside the other name

parts.note: Ben-Hur is the epic novel and film, so Ben's partner is Hur

indicators.note: break shakes the letters of the word loose into another order

parts.note: taken as written, its four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An aggressive person proposing a burglary at someone called Ben's place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' looks like a person but stands for the second half of Ben-Hur.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is an aggressively enterprising person who pushes deals on others.

clue.text: Landowner's shagged outside castle

indicators.note: outside means the slang word wraps round the chess piece

parts.note: laid is slang for having had sex, as shagged is in British slang
the castle is the rook in chess, R

explanation.surface: A landed gentleman has had sex just outside his castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: see13
Thumb Callow — that's hardly demurely feminine

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the English folk tale
callow and boyish both mean immature and youthful

explanation.surface: Sounds like a verdict on someone named Thumb Callow lacking ladylike manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboyish girl behaves in a rough, boisterous way thought typical of boys, the opposite of demure.

clue.text: Ridiculed, pissed, no Eye, without off-colour alternative

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the remaining letters wrap round the rest
no means the named word is dropped from the slang term

parts.note: in British slang pissed means drunk, and pie-eyed is another word for drunk
the magazine's name is taken as the plain word eye
off-colour means unwell, poorly
or is the word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A drunk being mocked, with a dig at Private Eye and its own off-colour humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' suggests a word containing PISS, but it is a synonym of drunk containing EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillory someone is to expose them to public scorn, as offenders once were in the pillory stocks.

clue.text: Tip: taking on computing stuff is to fulfil a death wish

parts.note: the tip of something is its end
IT, information technology, is computing

explanation.surface: Advice to take up computing as a way to bring on despair.
explanation.definitionFit: To end it all is the euphemism for suicide, the act a death wish craves.
